call_points.text: Management reiterated that H2 FY27 performance is expected to be better than H1 FY27.
Export LOIs include $430 million from CIS countries and $50 million from South East Asia, mostly in oil & gas.
Execution of 6 lakh MT job work order in Saudi Arabia remains delayed due to ongoing Middle East conflict.
Saudi JV with Buhur for longitudinal and helical pipe plants (300,000 MT each) is progressing land development and equipment LCs.
Pellet business profitability is impacted by higher stripping ratio, low Fe content in iron ore, and elevated diesel prices.
Surging coking coal costs squeezed margins in the ductile iron pipe segment during Q2.
Abu Dhabi DI pipe sales were restricted to 29,000 MT in Q2 (vs 34,000 MT in Q1) as sales are limited to truckable routes.
Next hearing for Jindal ITF vs NTPC litigation before the third judge of Delhi High Court is scheduled for January 2027.
FY27 pipe volumes expected flat on FY26 despite MENA disruption.
Q2 likely similar to Q1; H2 expected to improve over H1.
No domestic capacity additions planned; all expansion is in the Middle East.
Consolidated net institutional debt fell to ₹2,472 Cr from ₹2,528 Cr in March 2026.
Export order book ~60% Middle East, 40% non-Middle East.
MENA conflict and JJM delays named as key headwinds; API licence reinstated mid-June 2026.
Jindal ITF vs NTPC: Delhi High Court arguments closed, order reserved, expected within two months.
Export shipments to the MENA region have been suspended since March 1, 2026, due to force majeure from military conflict.
Q4 profitability was impacted by a ₹48 crore foreign exchange cost following the revaluation of US dollar-denominated exposures.
Total capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of ₹500 crores to ₹600 crores.
API monogram suspension on carbon seamless pipes is being addressed, with auditor verification scheduled for May 2026.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,633.48 Cr (-8.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹139.43 Cr (-52.1% YoY).
Board of Directors, led by **Sunil Kumar Jain (FCS-3056)**, recommended Rs. 2 final dividend per equity share (face value Rs. 1) for FY2026.
On April 27, 2026, Jindal Saw announced that its board approved in principle the disposal or liquidation of its wholly owned Cyprus subsidiary, Raleal Holdings Limited.
On April 27, 2026, Jindal Saw's board approved setting up an additional LSAW pipe plant in Saudi Arabia through its joint venture.
Sunil K. Jain, FCS-3056, informed BSE and NSE of the Q4FY26 conference call audio recording availability on April 28, 2026, via the company website.
Jindal Saw reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹4,657 Cr and PAT of ₹124 Cr, impacted by MENA export suspensions.
Jindal Saw Limited’s 41st AGM on May 29, 2026, approved all resolutions, including audited financial statements and dividend declaration, via electronic voting.

Jindal Saw Q1FY27 consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to ₹91 Cr on MENA shipment suspension and weak water demand; management guided flat FY27 volumes and term debt rising to ~₹3,500 Cr for Middle East plants.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,471.79 Cr (+5.6% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹47.04 Cr (-69.0% YoY).
Sunil K. Jain hosted Q2FY27 conference call on October 19, 2026, with audio recording available at jindalsaw.com.
In its Q2FY27 earnings call, Jindal Saw highlighted a total order pipeline of ~₹17,000 Cr including $625 Mn in non-MENA LOIs, and reiterated H2 FY27 performance will improve over H1 FY27.
